findings.title: Return type change breaks callers
findings.body: The function `until_service` changed its return type from `int` to `tuple[int, int]`, but the planner in `fleetlog/planner.py` line 14 compares the result directly to `SERVICE_WINDOW_KM` using `>`. This will raise a `TypeError` at runtime because a tuple cannot be compared to an integer.

findings.title: Comparison against tuple return value
findings.body: The planner compares the result of `until_service(vehicle_id)` directly to `SERVICE_WINDOW_KM` using `>`, but `until_service` now returns a tuple `(km_left, days_left)`. This will raise a `TypeError` at runtime. Update the comparison to use the first element of the tuple, e.g., `until_service(vehicle_id)[0] > SERVICE_WINDOW_KM`.

summary.problem: The change to `until_service` breaks callers by altering its return type without updating dependent code.
summary.done_well: The new function computes both kilometers and days left until service, improving the information available.
